**Still reproducing on v1.4.11 — and the live log contradicts the obvious "busy_timeout was 0" diagnosis.**

I filed this originally against `opencode run` (headless), but it's now surfacing in interactive TUI sessions too. Wanted to share fresh evidence in case it helps pin down the exact path.

### The smoking gun

```
ERROR 2026-04-18T02:50:17 +5015ms service=session.processor sessionID=… messageID=… error=database is locked stack=SQLiteError: database is locked
```

The `+5015ms` is the critical bit: `busy_timeout = 5000ms` **is** being honored on the failing connection — the writer just held the WAL lock for longer than 5s. A single `~/.local/share/opencode/log/2026-04-17T234221.log` from my install has 28 of these in one session. So this is a writer-duration problem, not a "timeout not set" problem. That reframes the fix — bumping `busy_timeout` alone won't help if a large bash-tool output takes 8s to serialize into `part`.

### What a fresh CLI connection actually shows

```
$ sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "PRAGMA busy_timeout;"
0
```

I'd read this as "some code path opens without applying the default" — but the `+5015ms` log contradicts that, so it's more likely that `PRAGMA busy_timeout` is session-local (expected) and the failing connection *did* have 5000ms set. The `0` just reflects the CLI's own new connection, not opencode's runtime state. Leaving this here because if anyone else repros with `sqlite3` they'll see the same `0` and draw the wrong conclusion.

### A single interactive TUI is already multi-writer

```
$ lsof ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db | awk 'NR>1 {print $2}' | sort -u | wc -l
11
$ lsof ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db | wc -l
24   # incl. header
```

11 opencode PIDs, 23 FDs on one DB file. A single TUI holds multiple FDs on `opencode.db` concurrently, so even with only one "user-visible session", the app is competing against itself for the single WAL writer slot. Any 9-13 pane workload amplifies this. I suspect this is why the per-session-tree sharding idea in #20935 and PR #21579 would help even for solo users.

### Current DB profile (context for anyone repro'ing)

- `opencode.db`: **1.3 GB** (1,314,107,392 bytes)
- `message`: 60,123 rows
- `part`: 168,942 rows
- Free pages: ~0% (VACUUM isn't the main win here — lock-hold time is)

### User-visible failure mode (the biggest quality-of-life ask)

When a lock fires, the session halts with the error banner and there's no automatic retry. I have to reload the thread and sometimes lose the in-flight tool call. An **exponential-backoff retry on `SQLITE_BUSY` in the write path** (50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s → give up) would make almost all of these invisible without changing the architecture. That would buy time while the larger sharding work in #20935/#21579 lands.

### Related upstream threads

- #21000 — bash tool hanging on large output, which I suspect is the common lock-duration trigger
- #20935 — per-session-tree DB sharding (feature request)
- #21579 — sharding implementation PR (happy to test against a real 9-13 pane workload if useful)

### What I'm shipping on my side (mitigation only)

Weekly `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` + conditional `VACUUM` + `PRAGMA optimize` via a maintenance routine, scheduled off-hours. Doesn't touch busy_timeout or retry — those can only be fixed in opencode itself. Code: [marcusquinn/aidevops#19630](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/19630) if useful as a reference for what external tooling can and can't do.

Happy to supply a full log sample or run instrumented builds if it would help.

hit this same shape shipping a couple MCP servers into opencode and Claude Code. one gotcha beyond just moving resolveTools past mcp.tools(): MCP tool names get namespaced (server_name + tool_name), so your permission patterns probably don't match what the LLM actually sees. if you fix the ordering but keep exact-name matching, dynamic tools added at runtime still slip through. wildcard prefix matching on the namespaced name, run through the same Permission.disabled filter as built-ins, is what worked for us.

Bumping this with some context to help prioritize:

This PR follows the same pattern as #14586 (merged), which fixed empty content crashes for Bedrock by filtering empty strings. That fix closed #11210. This PR closes the gap for a second code path (the interleaved reasoning filter) which can also produce `content: []` on Bedrock, but runs *after* the existing guard so it was never caught.

Evidence it's a real pain point:
- #22364, #15715, #16332 are all open Bedrock `ValidationException` reports; some may be hitting this exact path
- #14638 documents interleaved reasoning breakage on non-Claude Bedrock models
- Live-verified on `amazon-bedrock/zai.glm-4.7`: crashes at step 14 before fix, completes 199 steps after

The fix is 2 lines. PR is rebased to current dev, all 6 new tests pass, 0 regressions across the existing transform suite.

**Update:** Improved the orphan indicator UX: - The `! orphan` label in the footer was misleading — it looked like a keybind, as if pressing `!` would "orphanize" a session - Replaced it with a contextual note at the bottom: `NOTE: ! means the session is orphan` - The note is only shown when orphaned sessions are actually present in the list - The `!` in the note is displayed in the same warning color as the gutter indicator for consistency

This is an umbrella root-cause issue, not a duplicate report. The referenced issues (#15715, #16332, #17705, #22364) are all symptoms of the same architectural gap: the `message()` pipeline has no final empty-content validation step, so any transformation pass that produces `content: []` or `content: ""` silently passes through to the provider.

Each of those issues was filed against a specific provider or scenario. This issue identifies the common cause across all of them and tracks PR #23259, which adds a single guard at the end of the pipeline that fixes all current and future cases in one place.

Looked at the source with Claude — turns out you can just add

```json
"mouse": true
```

to `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` so it looks like this (create the file if needed):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "mouse": true
}
```

Restart opencode and it works.

Tested with MiniMax-M2.5 on macOS in iTerm2 — does exactly what's asked for in this issue: scroll up (wheel or PageUp) pauses sticky, scroll back to the bottom resumes it.

Thanks for the review @Brendonovich — you're right, the sidecar CLI is gone. I see `spawnLocalServer` now imports `virtual:opencode-server` and calls `Server.listen()` in-process, so there's no separate child process to leak anymore.

That said, the `window-all-closed` handler is still missing. On macOS, closing the last window leaves the Electron app running in the dock with the in-process server still consuming memory — the user has to Cmd+Q or Force Quit to actually free resources. Since there's no dock menu to reopen the window, the app just sits there invisible and unreachable.

Would it still make sense to add the `window-all-closed → quit` behavior so closing the window actually releases resources? Happy to update the PR description to reflect the current architecture if so, or close it if you'd prefer to handle this differently.
